intro: Project managers already run budgets, schedules and teams, so many management roles are within reach. The closest of the 25 careers below is Information Technology Project Managers, with a 96% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $116,580 for the broader computer and information systems group.
why_it_works: Your work is keeping people, deadlines and risks in line. O*NET rates judgment at 3.62 and coordination at 3.5 out of 5 for this job, which is why administrative, operations and training managers come out so close. All 25 matches need no extra education. The usual gap is deeper operations knowledge: analyzing processes, monitoring operations and owning a budget rather than tracking it.
tips: Quantify finished projects: budget size, team size and how often you delivered on time are what hiring managers scan for.
If you lean toward tech, Computer and Information Systems Managers earn $175,140, or 71% more than your current median.
Ask to own part of a budget now, since financial management is one of the main gaps in your matches.

faq.q: What jobs can former project management specialists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are IT project managers (96%), Administrative Services Managers (90%) and General and Operations Managers (90%), based on O*NET 31.0 data. Administrative Services Managers earn a median of $114,130, which is 12% more than the $102,320 project specialist median.

faq.q: Which careers for project managers pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more than $102,320. The biggest gains are Computer and Information Systems Managers at $175,140 (71% more), Financial Managers at $166,570 (63% more) and Marketing Managers at $166,790 (63% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do project management specialists need another degree?
faq.a: No for every match on this page: all 25 usually need no more education than project specialists already have. A bachelor's degree is common in the closest roles, held by 38% of workers, so experience and results matter more than a new diploma.

faq.q: What skills should project managers build next?
faq.a: Across the top matches, the skills that most often need work are operations analysis, operations monitoring, managing financial resources and operation and control. Time management already rates 3.5 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so the gap is running operations, not organizing them.
